messages:
arian: thinking out loud — we need a documented safety-net protocol for the continuous batcher. not just eviction rules but a slowpath that guarantees progress when coalescing fails.

mika: agreed. current fallbacks are ad-hoc. proposals?

jordan: what I had in mind: a two-tier fallback. first: soft-reject/admit-to-slowpath (best-effort shorter batch window). second: hard-escape that routes to single-request fastpath with stricter kv-warmup heuristic.

sophia: +1. important to include headroom accounting so slowpath doesn't create a runaway tenant on fastpath. we need a credit debit model.

arian: sketch: every tenant has a soft headroom token pool and a slowpath budget. when coalesce fails for >X ms, we consume slowpath budget and move requests to fastpath until budget drains. budget replenishes slowly.

mika: how do we measure "coalesce fails"? queue growth, observed latency, or failing to form a batch within Nms?

jordan: prefer: no batch formed in Nms OR observed per-queue in-flight > threshold. combine signals. keep it simple at first.

sophia: telemetry question — we must emit a tag on requests that took slowpath so Optimize/Console can correlate LLM-quality regressions. otherwise ops will be blind.

arian: note: slowpath must still honor KV cache warmup. we should bias slowpath to requests with smaller prefix lengths to avoid cold kv blowup. add prefix-length hint to admission.

mika: what about fairness? if one tenant hits slowpath and steals fastpath capacity, others suffer. headroom tokens should be globally normalized by tenant commit tier. reserved capacity tenants get larger budgets.

jordan: implementation detail: admission controller should return an enum: {COALESCE_OK, SLOWPATH_REQUESTED, FASTPATH_ESCALATED}. runtime uses that to pick pipeline. keep API stable.

sophia: +1 on explicit enum. helps observability and rollout. also, add a reason string for metrics.

arian: we also need a mutual backpressure handshake between batcher and scheduler: when slowpath budgets are low, batcher signals downstream to preemptively flush micro-windows. avoid surprise long tails.

mika: how to avoid oscillation? if we flush too eagerly, we increase cost; if we flush too late, tails explode. hysteresis with min-flush-interval?

jordan: use damping: require N consecutive slow signals before full flush; allow one-off bleed-throughs. also exponential backoff for budget replenishment to discourage repeated bursts.

sophia: testing plan: simulate 1000 tenants with power-law request sizes, enable slowpath on 10% tenants, and validate latency SLOs for p50/p99. add unit tests for enum surface and a chaos test which randomly drops coalescing.

arian: rollout plan: feature-flag the slowpath and headroom accounting behind a cluster-opt-in. start with dedicated pools (non-hosted) to watch cost. enable metric exports: slowpath_rate, fastpath_escalations, headroom_balance per tenant.

mika: ops runbook snippet: if fastpath_escalations spike, look for bursty tenants, throttle their slowpath budget, and enable temporary tenant cap. avoid mass rollback.

jordan: corner case: streaming requests that are mid-run — if a request is moved to slowpath mid-assembly, we must preserve partial KV cache and resume seamlessly. requires portable resume tokens.

sophia: portable resume tokens are already a future item we debated. add an incremental token that captures KV pointers + prefix length + partial logits. minimal shape.

arian: open questions for next RFC follow-up: 1) exact budget replenishment curve params, 2) how to encode prefix-length hint in the API ergonomically, 3) knobs for reserved capacity tenants vs host-tiered.

mika: can we prototype with a simple leaky-bucket budget curve and default params: capacity=1000 credits, refill=10 credits/sec, slowpath cost=50 credits/request? tweak after simulation.

jordan: I'll spin up a small sim and post numbers. aim to keep p50 unaffected and p99 stable within 10% of baseline.

sophia: I'll add telemetry fields to the console schema and a dashboard wireframe.

ci-bot: deploy-checklist: PRs needed -> batcher:admission-enum, scheduler:headroom-accounting, runtime:fastpath-funnel, telemetry:slowpath-metrics. required reviewers: @arian @mika @jordan @sophia.

arian: thanks — good progress. will consolidate into an RFC follow-up doc with diagrams and the sim results.
